statusHistory.note: London war-room slate (BACKLOG.md / content/post-plan.md). NITE-PORTER draft, English only. Verified via the hotel's own site, Wikipedia, and two independent reviews (Mr & Mrs Smith, Tripping On Travel): address 6 Frith Street, Soho Square, W1D 3JA; Georgian building dating to 1718, spread across three interconnected townhouses; William Hazlitt died in the house in 1830, blue plaque by the front door; no exterior hotel signage (Condé Nast Traveller, quoted on the hotel's own site: 'There's nothing outside to indicate that this is a hotel'); 30 rooms (3 singles, 24 doubles, 2 junior suites, 1 suite); rooms named for Hazlitt's circle; no lift, creaky stairs and a wonky top-floor landing consistently reported across reviews; resident cat (Sir Godfrey) and an honesty bar in the library per Mr & Mrs Smith. Rates 'from £329/night' per Mr & Mrs Smith at time of writing — treated as indicative, not quoted as current in the body. Currently operating (part of the same ownership as The Rookery and Batty Langley's). NOT verified: exact current nightly rates, whether accessibility features have changed, staff-side details (this is nite-porter's usual register but no staff-sourced quote was found — flagged rather than invented). Status held at draft: no hero image sourced yet (needs a near-illustrator pass — no rights-clear Wikimedia Commons photo of the actual building was found), and no other locale has been written. Geocode is an approximate manual placement for 6 Frith Street and needs refinement against a real geocoder before this goes live.
near-illustrator pass: found a genuinely usable, rights-clear exterior photo of the actual building on Wikimedia Commons (2011, CC BY-SA 3.0). Set as hero with strategy 'source'.
